messages.subject: Subsetting a reactive conductor
parts:
Hi,

Preamble: I am a beginner in the Shiny environment (but not with R in general). So please, bear with me if my question appears trivial and if I used the wrong lingo.

So I made this function to process session$clientData$url_search and that returns a list object. It is called within server.R as follows:
local <- reactive(myf(session$clientData$url_search))

Further down, I need to independently access to each slot of the list returned by myf... but local is a reactive conductor object, and that;s where my problem begin.

I created a simple app below to illustrate the problem, which can be summed up by: what is the proper syntax for "output$component <- ?" ?

output$component <- local$localData
returns
Error in local$localData : object of type 'closure' is not subsettable

output$component <- local()$localData
returns
Error in .getReactiveEnvironment()$currentContext() :
Operation not allowed without an active reactive context. (You tried to do something that can only be done from inside a reactive expression or observer.)

If I set the code as "local <- myf(1)" without reactive(), my app does not even start and I get:
Error in .getReactiveEnvironment()$currentContext() :
  Operation not allowed without an active reactive context. (You tried to do something that can only be done from inside a reactive expression or observer.)

I am confused...

Thanks in advance for your help




library(shiny)
library(shinydashboard)

myf <- function(x){
  list(a=x,
       b=letters[1:10],
       c=TRUE)
}

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  myconductor <- reactive(myf(1))
  output$component <- myconductor()$a
}

ui <- dashboardPage(
  header=dashboardHeader(),
  sidebar=dashboardSidebar(),
  body=dashboardBody(
    verbatimTextOutput('component')
  ),
  title='Test',
  skin='blue'
)

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Subsetting a reactive conductor
parts:
Every output function you call from the UI has a corresponding render function. In this case, verbatimTextOutput has renderText.

output$component <- renderText({
local()$localData
})

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Subsetting a reactive conductor
parts:
You may never access the value of a reactive expression/conductor, nor a reactive value, from outside of either:
  • A reactive expression/conductor, or
  • An observer
This may feel like a limitation but it's actually a feature--as in almost 100% of cases, if you're trying to read a reactive expression or value from outside one of those contexts, it's because of a misunderstanding of reactive programming.

In your example:

if (myconductor()$c){
    output$component <- renderText(paste(myconductor()$a, collapse=','))
  } else {
    output$component <- renderText(paste(myconductor()$b, collapse=','))
  }

The value of myconductor() will change over time--this is the nature of reactive expressions. But this code will run only once. Instead, you need to invert the logic to this:

output$component <- renderText({
  if (myconductor()$c) {
    paste(myconductor()$a, collapse=",")
  } else {
    paste(myconductor()$b, collapse=",")
  }
})

Don't think of assignment to output$whatever as saying "update the value of this output to xxx", but rather, "here is the RECIPE for how you would update the output, I'll let you (the framework) worry about when and how often to actually perform the update".

I highly recommend that you work through the "Effective reactive programming" videos here: https://www.rstudio.com/resources/webinars/shiny-developer-conference/ At the very least, you will find Part 1 very helpful I think.
